$comment: The exact set of source modules the coverage gates hold, as web-root-relative posix paths, the per-file thresholds they are held to, and the coverage configuration the run must RESOLVE. ONE manifest, read by two independent checks: src/guards.test.ts asserts that the minimatch derivation from vitest.config.ts's coverage.include/exclude produces exactly `coverageGated`, that `thresholds` equals both its own literal EXPECTED_COVERAGE_THRESHOLDS and vitest.config.ts's coverage.thresholds, and that `resolvedCoverage` agrees with the same literals plus vitest.config.ts's `globalSetup` and `test.include` (config vs manifest); and scripts/assert-coverage-scope.mjs asserts that the config vitest RESOLVED for the run -- captured from vitest's own resolved config by the globalSetup module, overrides folded in -- deep-equals `resolvedCoverage`, that the coverage report that run actually wrote lists exactly `coverageGated`, and that each of those modules' recomputed percentages meet `thresholds` (runtime vs manifest). Neither check can be satisfied by editing the other's source: the config-side deep-equal catches an edit to vitest.config.ts, and the runtime side catches a CLI flag or plugin config() hook that changes the resolved config without touching any source the first side reads. `resolvedCoverage.coverage` is deep-equalled WHOLE, every key of it, because binding one more coverage key each round is how three successive reviews each found the next unbound one -- the file set, then the thresholds, then the provider. Adding a genuinely new gated module, moving a threshold, or changing any resolved coverage option therefore requires a reviewed edit to this file -- that human-review latch is deliberate, not an oversight. It cannot be edited into permissiveness: scripts/assert-coverage-scope.mjs's readCoverageScope applies the same invariants to `resolvedCoverage` that it applies to the captured config (v8 provider, no customProviderModule, coverage enabled, all:true, a json reporter, usable per-file thresholds equal to `thresholds`), so a manifest that licenses a custom provider throws instead. It is not the only pin on today's 24 modules: src/guards.test.ts also names several of them in literal assertions (`scan scope > coverage-gates exactly the modules coverage-scope.json lists` names src/api/qvpc.ts, src/api/client.ts, src/scene/color.ts, src/scene/shaders/orbitalPoints.ts, src/components/Inspector.tsx and src/state/useSceneStore.ts, and the gate fixtures below it name more), which is why a coordinated edit to vitest.config.ts, the canonical arrays and this file still fails the build. Those literals cover only the modules they name; a module added later and quietly removed again is caught by the latch alone. `pragmaScanned` is `coverageGated` plus the type-only modules that carry no per-file threshold but are still scanned for coverage-ignore pragmas -- 25 entries, the 24 gated modules plus src/api/types.ts, which is the ONLY excluded module and is held to being genuinely type-only by `committed suite integrity > keeps the modules coverage excludes as type-only actually type-only`. As of PR-8A `coverage.include` is `src/**/*.ts` + `src/**/*.tsx`, i.e. every production module under src/: the React/three layer (src/components/, src/state/, the .tsx scene components, App.tsx, main.tsx) is inside the gate rather than outside it, which closes the documented re-export escape -- moving a gated module's body into an unmeasured directory and leaving a one-line re-export no longer hides anything, because there is no unmeasured directory left under src/.

resolvedCoverage.$comment: Written by scripts/capture-resolved-coverage.mjs from vitest's resolved `project.config`, normalised: reportsDirectory is made root-relative (and case-folded on Windows, where `COVERAGE` and `coverage` are one directory) and processingConcurrency (min(20, availableParallelism())) is replaced by a marker, because both differ between machines -- their KEYS are still pinned. A marker is an object with the single key `__captured`, never a string: a string marker could not be told apart from a genuine string value spelled the same way. `coverage.exclude` is longer than vitest.config.ts's coverage.exclude on purpose: vitest appends the resolved setupFiles and `test.include` to it (resolveConfig, coverage.DfSpMS-b.js:3664-3668), so the last two entries are test.include and src/guards.test.ts binds them to it. The capture also carries `coverageProviderName` (the provider OBJECT vitest loaded) and the gate holds it to "v8" absolutely -- that is one more layer, not a wall: a fake provider that declares `name = 'v8'` satisfies it, and everything captured here is written by the same trust domain it describes -- one mutable, equally-privileged checkout, which cannot vouch for itself. See docs/project/status.md, "门禁的防护边界".
